newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up, banks in short dollar stance.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up, banks in short dollar stance.

text.p: The won ended Thursday's trading higher against the dollar after banks began taking short dollar positions, traders said.
The won ended at 828.70 after opening at 829.40. It ranged from 828.10 to 830.10.

"The market tried the 830 level several times in the past week, but it didn't succeed penetrating it," said a Chase Manhattan Bank dealer. "So major banks felt the suitable level was lower and began shorting their positions."
This prompted stop-loss selling by other banks, further undermining the U.S. unit, he added.
